newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - INDIAN NEWSPAPERS - AUG 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - INDIAN NEWSPAPERS - AUG 7.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
All Papers
PRIME MINISTER DEALT SETBACK OVER INSURANCE BILL

Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral suffered a humiliating setback when his minority government failed to muster enough votes in parliament to defeat an amendment barring foreign insurance firms. Gujral abruptly withdrew an insurance regulatory bill when it became clear his government did not have enough votes to defeat the opposition-backed amendment.
Indian Express
CONGRESS PARTY TO THINK OF JOINING GOVERNMENT

The Congress party session in Calcutta might discuss a move to join the government. A section of the ruling United Front thinks the Congress party, with its 144 MPs, should join the coalition government to give it the stability it needs. There is a growing opinion in the party that either it join the government or function as an effective opposition. The second suggestion would mean an end to the Gujral government.
The Hindustan Times
LALOO YADAV LANDS IN HOSPITAL

Former Bihar chief minister Laloo Prasad Yadav pleaded ill health and did not appear before a court that is hearing the fodder case. He was admitted to the Indira Gandhi Institute of Medical Sciences after he complained of chest heaviness, stomach disorder, uneasiness and hypertension. Laloo Yadav and 54 other accused in the case were to appear before the court on Wednesday.
The Economic Times
CHIDAMBARAM SAYS INSURANCE BILL COULD BE SAVED

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said the Insurance Regulatory Authority bill could still be saved if the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) considered his amendment that registration might be granted only to Indian insurance companies. He said the amendment proposed by the BJP was outside the scope of the Act. The BJP wanted an amendment barring foreign companies from doing insurance business in India. Chidambaram said the General Insurance Corporation operated in about 35 countries and the BJP amendment would only send the wrong signals to the world.
JET AIRWAYS TO BY PARTNERS' STAKES

Jet Airways chairman Naresh Goyal will buy the stakes of Gulf Air and Kuwait Airways which together hold 40 percent of Tail Winds, the holding company of Jet Airways registered in the Isle of Man. Sources said the negotiations were on and a deal would be struck by the first week of October. The share price has not yet been fixed.
Financial Express
NINTH PLAN POWER POLICY AIMS AT FOREIGN DIRECT INVESTMENT

The government is modifying its power policy to attract private and overseas investments. During the Ninth Plan the focus will be on small projects with shorter gestation periods. The additional capacity target will be lowered to 39,000 megawatts instead of the earlier target of 56,000 megawatts. Attempts will be made to improve the plant load factor and reduce transmission and distribution losses.
C.K. BIRLA ROPES IN MCKINSEY

C.K. Birla has appointed international consultants McKinsey to strengthen the functioning of the group companies and shore up bottom lines. The focus will be to evolve a cost-cutting business strategy for the group's main businesses which include cement and automobiles, sources said. McKinsey is likely to study the Mitsubishi Lancer auto project being carried out near Madras by the Hindustan Motors. The consultants will also try to fix benchmarks for products.
MAURITIUS BANS SEAFOOD IMPORT FROM INDIA

Mauritius banned seafood imports from India, saying they are unhygienic. The European Union has already banned Indian seafood for the same reason. But it has agreed to a review meeting to be held on August 7 in Brussels. The Commerce Ministry now fears that the United States and Japan may also ban Indian seafood. The ministry identified 18 seafood exporting units which are eligible to export to the European Union since they met the stringent hygiene standard. It has sought time until August 15 from the European Union to inspect and ensure that the units meet the hygiene standards.
NATIONAL BOURSE ALLOWS BROKER CARD TRANSFERS

The National Stock Exchange (NSE) decided to allow the transfer of memberships from one trading member to another. Until now it only allowed reconstitution of management. The NSE amended its rule to allow such transfers. Members applying for transfer of cards will have to pay a transfer fee of 2.5 million rupees. But the fee will be charged only in cases where the trading member has nominated someone other than a successor.
The Observer
GOVERNMENT TO OFFLOAD EQUITY IN THREE MORE COMPANIES

The Disinvestment Commission in its fourth report to the government has recommended the sale of government equity in three public sector undertakings -- Hindustan Copper, the Pawan Hans Helicopters and Shipping Corporation. The Commission's chief said the panel had suggested that the Power Grid Corporation's disinvestment should be kept in abeyance until the entire power sector is restructured.
